scope: Milestone C on-device verification of the Android companion client's command bar: the fixed key row (navigation keys plus Ctrl chords) and the snippet row below the stage, exercised live on the phone's cover screen through the ADB loopback harness. Finish line per spec: ^C verifiably interrupts a running program (exercised, not assumed) and snippets round-trip across process death.

checks.interrupt: send 'busy' through the composer, wait for the program's numbered output, swipe the key row until the ^C chip is on screen, tap it; the PTY line discipline turns the byte into SIGINT and the program reports 'busy interrupted after N lines'; the agent then answers a follow-up line, proving the session is alive after the interrupt
checks.snippets: tap + to open the editor, type a snippet, Add, Done; the chip appears in the bar with the saved text and tapping it sends paste+Enter (the fake agent echoes the line); force-stop and plain relaunch restores the chip from DataStore with the right text

defects_found_and_fixed: The snippet editor's test tags never reached uiautomator: AlertDialog opens its own window, so the root-level testTagsAsResourceId set in MainActivity does not apply to the dialog's composition, and the harness could not address any node inside it by resource id (the dialog itself opened and worked). Fixed by setting testTagsAsResourceId on the editor column and the Done button inside the dialog.

The busy workload first ran denser (a line every 150 ms) and uiautomator could not dump the window at all — the phone-side observation channel goes blind on a window redrawing that fast, which surfaced as a false 'the busy program never started' while the program was actually running. Slowed to one line per 1.5 s so dumps have quiet windows; the interrupt itself was always delivered.

The scrollback check left the terminal surrendered from follow-bottom (a drag landed off the live row), so later checks could not see new output. The check now scrolls back down to the live bottom before finishing and fails loudly ('scrolling never returned to the live bottom') if the prompt is not the last visible row.

PR review round found eight more issues, all fixed together: snippet bounds were enforced only at load, not at edit or save (now one SnippetStore.normalize projection shared by the bar, the editor, save, and reload, with an invariant test); DataStore threw IOException/CorruptionException into Main-dispatcher coroutines where UserDefaults is best-effort (the Settings seam now absorbs read and write failures for every key); commandBarEnabled/snippets state, the editor-open flag, and the editor's uncommitted rows and draft used plain remember so a fold recreation dropped them (rememberSaveable throughout, the row list via an explicit listSaver); the wide FlowRow had no vertical spacing and long snippet chips could wrap and grow the bar (verticalArrangement plus one-line ellipsized chips); the interrupt check leaked a running busy program on failure paths (try/finally best-effort ^C); the snippets check reused text across runs so a stale chip could satisfy the assertion (run-unique text) and assumed an empty editor (clears existing rows first); chip padding sat outside the click modifier so the visible chip border was dead to touches (padding now inside the clickable); and saved settings applied after first composition so a session opened at default geometry then resized (fit() gated on settingsLoaded).

Two later review findings, also fixed: chip padding was applied outside the click modifier, so the tap target was only the glyph and the visible padded chip border was dead to touches (padding now follows the click modifier inside it); and saved settings applied after first composition, so a session opened at the default font and bar visibility and resized a moment later when the saved values landed (fit() is now gated on a settingsLoaded flag set by the one effect that reads font size, bar visibility, and snippets, so the first open happens at the configured geometry).

A fourth review round (13 findings, all addressed): reveal() judged chip containment against wm-size panel width, which can report the unfolded panel while the cover display is in use, and swiped a fixed row height instead of the chip's own row (now judged against the command-bar node's own right edge and swiped at the chip's own vertical center, returning None when the bar itself is absent so callers name that failure); a failed interrupt left the busy program owning the PTY so the background and snippets checks failed with messages blaming the wrong interaction (a wedged flag now makes later PTY-typing checks report SKIPPED, recorded in the receipt, and fake_agent treats a stray ^C at the idle prompt as a no-op so the harness's best-effort second ^C cannot kill the fixture); the snippets check opened the editor through the + chip, which is off-screen once any snippet persists (the always-visible first chip's long-press opens the same editor); a second attached adb device could silently steal the run (--serial is now mandatory with more than one device); settingsLoaded was set only on the success path so an unexpected throwable in the reads would leave a stage that never opens (set in finally — opening at default geometry beats never opening); the settings effect keyed on fontSizeOverride so a debug-intent change re-ran the store loads and could revert a snippet save still in flight (keyed on settings, override read via rememberUpdatedState); setSnippets was a fresh unstable lambda each composition defeating CommandBar skippability (remembered like onInput); the settings toggle was flippable during the one frame before the DataStore read landed, which could write the default over a saved off (Switch disabled until commandBarLoaded); the editor rejected over-length pastes with no visible feedback (monospace n / 512 counters under each field); and the evidence receipt described commits and runs in prose (now explicit SHAs and commands).
limitations: Ctrl chords other than ^C (^D ^U ^L ^R ^Z ^W) are unit-tested as raw control-byte payloads but not individually exercised on device; ^C is the spec's named finish line and its SIGINT path through the PTY is the same wire shape all chords use.
The compact-width scrollable strip is what the cover screen exercises; the expanded FlowRow layout at >=840dp awaits milestone D's unfolded-display gate, as does any posture-docked placement.

Snippet persistence is per-device DataStore; the settings hide/show toggle is implemented and tagged but its UI interaction is not an automated check row (the bar's presence is asserted indirectly by every key/snippet check).
Transport remains the adb-reverse loopback with the fake_agent fixture; the real-Codex overlay run is still folded into the milestone A/D gates.
